newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end sharply down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end sharply down on profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks continued their fall for the second straight day on Thursday to close sharply lower on across the board profit-taking, brokers said.
The all share index closed 15.28 points lower at 730.32 on turnover of 108.7 million rupees.
Price declines outnumbered gains by 66 to 14. Aitken Spence & Co fell eight rupees to 154, Bogawantalawa Plantations two rupees to 38, Commercial Bank 10 to 200.
"Profit-taking may continue until the all share comes closer to 700 points, when renewed buying will take it back up," said Manjula Kumarasinghe of brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.
Retail investors who had been starved of gains when Colombo stocks were inactive in 1996, were booking profits of over 50 percent in selected shares, brokers said.
"Retailers who are having a field day after so long are not about to give up yet," said Dimuthu Abeysekera of Allied Phillips Securities.
Brokers said they expected some more profit-taking on Friday.
